title: AHB System Ownership and Conservation Model
description: Execute arbitration/decode/response routing, bridge conservation, lock, exclusive, and security checkpoints without presenting one system policy as mandatory protocol behavior.
learnerQuestion: How do address owner, accepted target, data/response owner, bridge capacity, and policy state remain attributable?

configurations.label: AHB5 matrix path
configurations.description: One manager per layer with accepted target retimed into response ownership.

configurations.label: Original shared AHB
configurations.description: Arbitrated ownership with HLOCKx/HMASTLOCK and RETRY/SPLIT revision behavior.

scenarios.label: Arbitration and matrix resources
scenarios.description: Ownership changes only at the accepted handover boundary; concurrency and fairness depend on configured arbitration and matrix resources.

checks.label: Grant is not active ownership
checks.evidence: The active manager remains M0 until the protocol handover boundary.

steps.label: Different targets
steps.event: M0→S0 and M1→S1 on separate matrix layers

checks.label: Separate layers may progress
checks.evidence: Matrix concurrency follows the implemented layers and target ports.

steps.label: Configured fairness
steps.event: Eligible M1 request waits behind higher-priority traffic

checks.label: Configured fairness bound
checks.evidence: AHB does not mandate this policy or bound; the assertion is gated by the product contract and environment assumptions.

scenarios.label: Retimed decode and response owner
scenarios.description: The next visible address can select SRAM while the current response still belongs to the accepted UART transfer.

checks.label: Exactly one accepted decode
checks.evidence: Accepted target selection is captured for the next data/response phase.

steps.label: Return UART
steps.event: Visible address selects SRAM; active response returns UART HREADYOUT/HRESP/HRDATA

checks.label: Response follows retimed owner
checks.evidence: The return mux uses accepted prior selection, not the current visible address decode.

scenarios.label: Unbuffered bridge conservation
scenarios.description: A bridge with one configured entry cannot accept a second AHB transfer until its downstream Setup/Access operation and upstream response retire the first.

checks.label: Bridge depth respected
checks.evidence: The unbuffered configuration backpressures rather than overwriting transaction state.

steps.label: Retire bridge
steps.event: Downstream ACCESS completes and upstream data/response completes

checks.label: One-in/one-out conservation
checks.evidence: No accepted transfer is lost or duplicated across the configured bridge.

scenarios.label: Lock, exclusive, and security state
scenarios.description: Distinct retained state proves resource ownership, monitored exclusivity, and configured access enforcement are not interchangeable.

steps.label: Lock ownership
steps.event: HLOCKx request becomes accepted HMASTLOCK ownership

checks.label: Active lock owner retained
checks.evidence: A future grant does not prematurely transfer the active locked resource.

steps.label: Exclusive interference
steps.event: Matching exclusive read then interfering write

checks.label: Failed exclusive has no side effect
checks.evidence: Monitor invalidation produces exclusive failure, not a lock or HRESP error.

steps.label: Security denial
steps.event: HNONSEC access denied by configured firewall

checks.label: Denied read leaks no secure data
checks.evidence: The configured enforcement point returns no protected payload.

checks.label: Denied write has no secure side effect
checks.evidence: Security policy is verified end-to-end rather than assumed at one topology block.
